study_design: Placebo-controlled randomized trial of folic acid supplementation
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Among the 643 men who were randomly assigned to placebo or supplementation with folic acid
reason: The randomized trial evaluates incident prostate cancer diagnoses overall. No aggressive, high-grade, advanced, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint is reported.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Among the 643 men who were randomly assigned to placebo or supplementation with folic acid, the estimated probability of being diagnosed with prostate cancer over a 10-year period was 9.7% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 6.5% to 14.5%) in the folic acid group and 3.3% (95% CI = 1.7% to 6.4%) in the placebo group (age-adjusted hazard ratio = 2.63, 95% CI = 1.23 to 5.65, Wald test P = .01).
estimate_classifications.reason: The hazard ratio concerns diagnosis of prostate cancer overall and is not identified as an aggressive endpoint.
